items.prompt: Which word is spelt wrongly? We went to the libary to find a book about volcanoes.

options.why: Went is spelt correctly.
Volcanoes is spelt correctly. Volcano adds -es in the plural.
About is spelt correctly.

hints: Read each word slowly, sound by sound.
Some words have a letter that people forget when they speak quickly.
Say library slowly: li-brar-y. How many r sounds do you hear?
items.explanation: The correct spelling is library, with an r after the b. It is easy to miss when you say the word quickly.

items.prompt: One word is spelt wrongly. Write it correctly. I recieved a letter from my penfriend.
hints: Look carefully at the order of the vowels in each word.
Remember the rule: i before e except after c, when the sound is ee.
Find the word with ie or ei in it.
items.explanation: Received follows the rule i before e except after c, when the sound is ee: re-c-ei-ved.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.why: Children is plural, so it needs were, not was.
Is is for one person or thing.
Children is already plural, so it does not need an s.

hints: Children means more than one child.
A plural subject needs a plural verb.
Choose between was and were for a plural subject.
items.explanation: Children is plural, so the verb must be plural too: the children were playing.

items.prompt: Which sentence keeps the same tense all the way through?

options.text: Yesterday we visited the zoo and saw the elephants.
Yesterday we visit the zoo and saw the elephants.
options.why: Visit is present tense, but yesterday needs the past.

options.text: Yesterday we visited the zoo and see the elephants.
options.why: See is present tense, but the sentence is about yesterday.

options.text: Yesterday we will visit the zoo and saw the elephants.
options.why: Will visit is the future, which does not fit yesterday.

hints: Yesterday tells you when this happened.
Both verbs need to be in the same tense.
Find the two verbs in each sentence. Are they both past tense?
items.explanation: Yesterday means the past, so both verbs are in the past tense: visited and saw.

items.prompt: One word is the wrong homophone. Write the correct word. The team lost there match on Saturday.
hints: One word sounds right but is spelt for a different meaning.
Ask whose match it was.
Find the word that should show belonging.
items.explanation: The match belongs to the team, so it should be their. There is about a place.

items.prompt: Sort the words: spelt correctly or spelt wrongly.
hints: These are words that many people find tricky.
Check double letters and the order of vowels carefully.
Start with necessary. Remember: one collar and two sleeves, one c and two s.
items.explanation: Necessary, definitely and tomorrow are correct. The correct spellings of the others are separate, believe and weird.

items.prompt: Which change makes this sentence better? The food was nice and the music was nice too.

options.why: This does not improve the sentence and is not needed.

options.text: Change the second nice to lively.

options.why: Without and, the two parts would not be joined properly.
The sentence is about the past, so was is correct.

hints: Notice which word is used twice.
Good writers avoid repeating a dull word and choose a more precise one.
Think of a word that describes music better than nice.
items.explanation: Nice is repeated and does not say much. Lively tells the reader exactly what the music was like.

items.prompt: Which is the best way to correct this sentence? The storm was loud we hid under the blanket.

options.text: The storm was loud, we hid under the blanket.
options.why: A comma alone cannot join two sentences.

options.text: The storm was loud, so we hid under the blanket.
The storm was loud we, hid under the blanket.
options.why: The comma splits we from hid.

options.text: The storm, was loud we hid under the blanket.
options.why: The comma splits the storm from was loud.

hints: There are two complete sentences joined together with nothing between them.
You can fix this with a full stop, or with a comma and a joining word.
Find where the first complete sentence ends.
items.explanation: Two complete sentences usually need a full stop between them or a joining word. A comma with so joins them correctly.

items.prompt: Proofread: every saturday my freind and I goes to the market. Choose all the mistakes.

options.why: Market is a common noun, so it does not need a capital letter.
I is correct here, because my friend and I are doing the action.

hints: Check capital letters, spelling and grammar one at a time.
Sentences and days of the week start with capital letters. The verb must agree with my friend and I.
Start with the first word of the sentence.
items.explanation: The correct sentence is: Every Saturday my friend and I go to the market. My friend and I is plural, so go is right.

items.prompt: Which version of the sentence is fully correct?

options.text: Me and Arif went to the beach, where we found three shells.
options.why: Me cannot be the subject of a sentence. Use Arif and I.

options.text: Arif and I went to the beech, where we found three shells.
options.why: A beech is a tree. The seaside is a beach.

options.text: Arif and I went to the beach, where we found three shells.
Arif and me went to the beach, where we found three shell.
options.why: Me should be I, and three needs the plural shells.

hints: Each wrong version has at least one small mistake.
Check the people at the start, the homophone and the plural one at a time.
Try saying each sentence with only the word I or me. Which sounds right: I went or me went?
items.explanation: Arif and I is the subject, beach is the seaside and three shells is plural. The other versions each have a mistake.

items.prompt: One word is wrong. Write it correctly. The childrens played in the park.
hints: Child is a special plural.
It does not take an s.
Think of the plural of man.
items.explanation: The plural of child is children, so "childrens" is wrong.

items.prompt: ___ going to bring ___ coats to the party because it is cold.
hints: One word means "they are".
One word shows that coats belong to them.
Say the sentence with "they are" in the first gap.
items.explanation: "They're" means they are, and "their" shows ownership of the coats.

items.prompt: Sort each mistake by its type.

items.text: It was definately a good idea.
We saw a dolphin at the beech.
Mum bought milk eggs and rice.
The boys was late for school.

hints: Spelling errors are wrong letters or wrong word.
Punctuation errors are missing marks.
Grammar errors are wrong verb forms.
items.explanation: Definately and beech are spelling mistakes, a missing question mark or commas is punctuation, and "I seen" or "boys was" is grammar.

items.prompt: Read: Last Saturday, Kofi and his dad go to the market. They bought fresh fish and a bunch of bananas. Kofi carried the bag home. Which sentence has a tense error?

options.why: "They bought" is correctly in the past tense.
"Kofi carried" is correctly in the past tense.
Check the verbs again. One of them is wrong.

hints: Last Saturday tells us it is past.
Check each verb.
Which verb is still in the present?
items.explanation: "Go" should be "went" because the paragraph is about last Saturday.

items.prompt: Proofread: yesterday we visit the museum with our class. It was verry big, and the guide showed us dinosaur bones. Choose all the mistakes.
hints: Check the start of the sentence.
Yesterday tells you the tense.
Check each word spelling.
items.explanation: The sentence needs a capital letter, past tense "visited" and correct spelling "very".

items.prompt: Write the word that should replace "a" in this sentence. Wulan put a hat, a bottle and a umbrella in her bag.
hints: Look at the sound at the start of umbrella.
We say "an" before a vowel sound.
The error is in the last item.
items.explanation: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we say "an umbrella".

items.prompt: Put the steps for proofreading in a sensible order.
items: Underline words that look or sound wrong.
Check the underlined words in a dictionary.
Read it once more to check.
hints: You must find mistakes before fixing them.
Checking comes before correcting.
Final reading goes last.
items.explanation: First find the problems, then check them, correct them, and finally read again.

items.prompt: Which change makes this paragraph better? Amara was happy. Amara was happy because it was her birthday. Amara was happy to see her friends.

options.text: Replace each "Amara was happy" with "Amara was glad".
options.why: This swaps one word for another but keeps the repeating.

options.text: Join the ideas: Amara was happy because it was her birthday and she saw her friends.

options.why: This removes all the information.
This keeps the repeating.

hints: Look for repeated words.
Good editing joins ideas.
Which option removes repeating while keeping the meaning?
items.explanation: Joining the ideas removes repeated words and keeps all the information.

items.prompt: Build the correct sentence. The coats belong to the children.
items.answer: Their coats were hanging by the door.
hints: Choose the word that shows belonging.
Their means belonging to them.
The sentence begins with that word.
items.explanation: "Their" shows that the coats belong to them. "There" is a place.

items.prompt: Several girls own the bags, and several teachers share the room. Which sentence is fully correct?

options.text: The girl's bags were in the teachers room.
options.why: The first apostrophe is wrong for more than one girl, and teachers' needs one.

options.text: The girls' bags were in the teachers' room.
The girls bags were in the teacher's room.
options.why: The apostrophe is missing in girls', and teacher's means one teacher.

options.text: The girl's bags were in the teachers' room.
options.why: Girl's means one girl.

hints: Check whether each owner is one or many.
Plural owners put the apostrophe after the s.
Both owners here are plural.
items.explanation: The bags belong to several girls and the room belongs to several teachers, so both need s'.

items.prompt: Which word is spelt wrongly? The hotel offered comfortable accomodation near the beach.

options.why: Hotel is spelt correctly.
Comfortable is spelt correctly.
Beach is spelt correctly.

hints: Three words are right and one is wrong.
Check double letters.
Accommodation has two c and two m.
items.explanation: The correct spelling is accommodation, with double c and double m.

items.prompt: Write the correct spelling of each wrong word.
head: Wrong word
Correct word
hints: Remember "i before e except after c" when the sound is ee.
Say each word slowly.
Until has only one l.
items.explanation: The correct spellings are receive, which, their and until.

items.prompt: How many mistakes are in this sentence? dewi and her freind walked too the shop
hints: Check capital letters, spelling, homophones and the end.
Count each type once.
The sentence has no full stop.
items.explanation: There are four mistakes: Dewi needs a capital, freind should be friend, too should be to, and a full stop is missing.

items.prompt: True or false: Every sentence should begin with a capital letter.
hints: What starts a sentence?
Capital letter.
Check the first letter.
items.explanation: Capital letters mark the start of sentences, as in The dog ran.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "We was late for school" has no grammar mistakes.
hints: Check the verb.
Which verb goes with we?
Were.
items.explanation: With we, use were, so the sentence is We were late for school.

items.prompt: True or false: The word "recieved" in the sentence "I recieved a letter" is a spelling mistake.
hints: Check the order of letters.
Remember the rule after c.
After c, this ee sound is spelt ei.
items.explanation: The correct spelling is received. The rule is i before e except after c, when the sound is ee.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The dog wagged it's tail" is correct.
hints: Does it is fit?
Try replacing it's with it is.
Its with no apostrophe.
items.explanation: It's means it is. Its without an apostrophe shows belonging, so the sentence should say its tail.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "She go to school every day" contains a verb mistake.
hints: Check the verb.
Add s or es.
She goes.
items.explanation: With she, a present tense verb usually ends in s, so it should be She goes to school every day.

items.prompt: True or false: Proofreading means writing the first draft of a text.
hints: When does proofreading happen?
After writing.
It is checking.
items.explanation: Proofreading means checking a finished piece of writing for mistakes.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "Their going to the park" contains a mistake.
hints: Try replacing their with they are.
Does it fit?
They're.
items.explanation: Their shows belonging. The sentence needs they're, meaning they are.
